ordered_diagnoses: Cholangiocarcinoma of the extrahepatic bile duct

s1.syndrome_frame: Right upper abdominal pain with mass and abnormal liver function
salient_findings: Heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa
key_facts: 64-year-old woman
2-month history of right upper abdominal pain
No nausea, vomiting, chills, or fever
Afebrile and oriented on examination
Right upper abdominal tenderness without rebound or palpable masses
No hepatosplenomegaly
Negative Murphy’s sign and shifting dullness
Elevated WBC count
Elevated CA19-9 level
Presence of gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening
Enhanced pancreatic echogenicity on ultrasonography
Lesion in the right hepatic lobe adjacent to the gallbladder fossa on CT
Multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes on CT

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of right upper abdominal pain, elevated CA19-9 level, and imaging findings of a lesion in the right hepatic lobe with mild intrahepatic bile duct dilatation are consistent with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The absence of a primary extrahepatic tumor and the presence of multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gallbladder cancer
rejected.why: While gallstones and gallbladder wall thickening are present, the primary lesion is in the liver, not the gallbladder, making gallbladder cancer less likely.

rejected.label: Hepatocellular carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's AFP level is within normal limits, and the imaging findings do not suggest a typical hepatocellular carcinoma appearance.

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma of the extrahepatic bile duct
rejected.why: The patient's imaging findings do not show a primary lesion in the extrahepatic bile duct, and no extrahepatic primary tumor was identified.

rejected.label: Hepatic metastasis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of a primary tumor outside the liver, making hepatic metastasis less likely.

gold: Primary squamous cell carcinoma of the liver
